newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish airport Skavsta expects daily cargo flight.
newsitem.headline: Swedish airport Skavsta expects daily cargo flight.

text.p: Sweden's Skavsta airport will invest around two million crowns in improving its cargo facilities and was expecting a new daily freight operation to start shortly, an airport spokesman said on Friday.

Skavsta marketing manager Peter Rogeman told Reuters that Dutch-based CSC (Cargo Service Centre) had taken over the paper work and the building of pallets for the airport's air cargo operations at the turn of the year.
Skavsta airport is located in Nykoping, Sweden, which is 100 kms southwest of Stockholm.
CSC was in charge of trucking goods to the airport and was investing in additional equipment, Rogeman said.
"They are rebuilding the terminal with new technical devices," Rogeman said. He could not give an exact figure on how much these investments were worth.
The airport would invest in a ramp which will allow trucks to drive onto the same level as the freight terminal.
"We are investing about two million crowns," he said.

Cargolux has been flying a Boeing 747-400 freighter version from Skavsta to Luxembourg and onto Huntsville, Alabama since October 1995. The aircraft left on Saturday mornings and had a capacity of around 120 tonnes, Rogeman said.
The airport handled 8,500 tonnes of cargo, not including trucked volumes, in 1996, Rogeman said.
This figure compares to 900 tonnes in 1994.

With the start of the new daily freighter operation, Rogeman said the airport expected to handle between 20,000 and 25,000 tonnes of cargo in 1997. He could not give any more details about the freight operation but said it would be announced soon.

Of the total freight the airport handled in 1996, Rogeman said around 5,000 tonnes was ad hoc charters, of which 95 percent was to China or Russia. More than half of this was telecommunications equipment, he said.

The airport can handle any kind of aeroplane since its 2,600 metre-long runway was broadened at the ends in 1995 to handle a Boeing 747. Its technical support equipment included a wide-bodied high loader, Rogeman said.
As the Swedish coast guard uses the terminal as its hub, the airport is open 24 hours every day of the year with customs staff on call. It has 3,500 square metres of cargo terminals.
